1. [Maximum mark: 5]
A geometric sequence has $u_4 = -70$ and $u_7 = 8.75$. Find the second term of the sequence.

2.text_clean:
2. [Maximum mark: 6]
The number of marathons that Audrey runs in any given year can be modelled by a Poisson distribution with mean $1.3$.
(a) Calculate the probability that Audrey will run at least two marathons in a particular year. [2]
(b) Find the probability that she will run at least two marathons in exactly four out of the following five years. [4]

3.text_clean:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]
The following diagram shows the graph of $y = f(x)$, $-3 \le x \le 5$.
[Graph: piecewise linear function through (-3,-3), (-1,-2), (0,-1), (1,0), (2,1), (3,4), (5,5) on a grid]
(a) Find the value of $(f \circ f)(1)$. [2]
(b) Given that $f^{-1}(a) = 3$, determine the value of $a$. [2]
(c) Given that $g(x) = 2f(x-1)$, find the domain and range of $g$. [2]

4.text_clean:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]
The following shape consists of three arcs of a circle, each with centre at the opposite vertex of an equilateral triangle as shown in the diagram.
[Diagram (not to scale): Reuleaux triangle formed by three arcs over a dashed equilateral triangle; height of shape marked 6 cm]
For this shape, calculate
(a) the perimeter; [2]
(b) the area. [5]

5.text_clean:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]
Consider the expansion of $(2+x)^n$, where $n \ge 3$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
The coefficient of $x^3$ is four times the coefficient of $x^2$. Find the value of $n$.

6.text_clean:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]
Let $P(z) = az^3 - 37z^2 + 66z - 10$, where $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}$.
One of the roots of $P(z) = 0$ is $3 + \mathrm{i}$. Find the value of $a$.

7.text_clean:
7. [Maximum mark: 6]
Runners in an athletics club have season's best times for the $100\text{ m}$, which can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean $11.6$ seconds and standard deviation $0.8$ seconds. To qualify for a particular competition a runner must have a season's best time of under $11$ seconds. A runner from this club who has qualified for the competition is selected at random. Find the probability that he has a season's best time of under $10.7$ seconds.

8.text_clean:
8. [Maximum mark: 8]
Eight boys and two girls sit on a bench. Determine the number of possible arrangements, given that
(a) the girls do not sit together; [3]
(b) the girls do not sit on either end; [2]
(c) the girls do not sit on either end and do not sit together. [3]

9.text_clean:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]
A body moves in a straight line such that its velocity, $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$, after $t$ seconds is given by $v = 2\sin\left(\frac{t}{10} + \frac{\pi}{5}\right)\csc\left(\frac{t}{30} + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ for $0 \le t \le 60$.
The following diagram shows the graph of $v$ against $t$. Point A is a local maximum and point B is a local minimum.
[Graph: v against t for 0 to 60; local maximum A near t = 7.5, v ~ 2.3; crosses t-axis near t = 25; local minimum B near t = 43, v ~ -2.4; crosses again near t = 57]
(a) (i) Determine the coordinates of point A and the coordinates of point B.
(ii) Hence, write down the maximum speed of the body. [5]
(b) The body first comes to rest at time $t = t_1$. Find
(i) the value of $t_1$;
(ii) the distance travelled between $t = 0$ and $t = t_1$;
(iii) the acceleration when $t = t_1$. [6]
(c) Find the distance travelled in the first $30$ seconds. [3]

10.text_clean:
10. [Maximum mark: 19]
A random variable $X$ has probability density function
$f(x) = \begin{cases} 3a, & 0 \le x < 2 \\ a(x-5)(1-x), & 2 \le x \le b \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ $\quad a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+,\ 3 < b \le 5$.
(a) Find, in terms of $a$, the probability that $X$ lies between 1 and 3. [4]
Consider the case where $b = 5$.
(b) Sketch the graph of $f$. State the coordinates of the end points and any local maximum or minimum points, giving your answers in terms of $a$. [4]
(c) Find the value of
(i) $a$;
(ii) $\mathrm{E}(X)$;
(iii) the median of $X$. [11]

11.text_clean:
11. [Maximum mark: 17]
The following diagram shows part of the graph of $2x^2 = \sin^3 y$ for $0 \le y \le \pi$.
[Graph: symmetric closed curve about the y-axis from (0,0) to (0, pi), widest near y = pi/2; region R to the right of the y-axis shaded]
(a) (i) Using implicit differentiation, find an expression for $\frac{dy}{dx}$.
(ii) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$. [8]
The shaded region $R$ is the area bounded by the curve, the $y$-axis and the lines $y = 0$ and $y = \pi$.
(b) Find the area of $R$. [3]
The region $R$ is now rotated about the $y$-axis, through $2\pi$ radians, to form a solid.
(c) By writing $\sin^3 y$ as $(1 - \cos^2 y)\sin y$, show that the volume of the solid formed is $\frac{2\pi}{3}$. [6]
